subject: HC approval: ML infra backfill & tradeoff options
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Headcount tradeoff & backfill approval for ML infra IC

Team —

Quick note: we have an unexpected vacancy on the ML Infrastructure IC track (SWE IV) after Jorge accepted another role. This role is critical to our low-latency serving roadmap (KV cache work + batching improvements). Given the hiring freeze, I am requesting an exception or a tradeoff path so we can maintain momentum on a few time-sensitive initiatives.

I attached a short tradeoff table (HC_Tradeoff_Table.xlsx) that lays out 3 options:
- Option A: Immediate backfill (1x SWE IV) — impact: keeps timelines, +$220k run-rate
- Option B: Delay backfill to Q3 and move contractor coverage (0.6 FTE equivalent) — impact: +3–4 week slippage, saves ~$110k this fiscal quarter
- Option C: Re-scope roadmap and distribute tasks across infra and model infra (internal reprioritization) — impact: reduces feature scope, saves ~$160k

Ask: please indicate whether you can support an exception for Option A, or whether we should pursue Option B and I will coordinate contractors/re-prioritization. I also included an initial org chart slice and a suggested interim owner for on-call.

Why this matters: the KV cache work is upstream of multiple customer-facing projects; delays will push out throughput gains that reduce per-token cost. If we defer hiring we should lock in a clear rollback and a re-eval cadence (30/60/90).

Attachments: HC_Tradeoff_Table.xlsx (spreadsheet), org_chart_v3.pdf (org slice)

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Group Product Manager, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Kaufman <elaine.kaufman@talentpartners.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Headcount tradeoff & backfill approval for ML infra IC

Hannah —

Thanks for the concise options. A couple of clarifying asks before I can sign off on an exception:
1) Prioritized task list for the next 12 weeks if we choose Option B (what absolutely must ship vs what can be delayed).
2) Updated org chart with interim escalation path (I see you attached a slice; can you include direct reports and dotted lines for support teams?).
3) Impact on commitments to three enterprise customers we promised throughput improvements to — if there are any dates that must not move, flag them.

Elaine — looping you in to understand timeline for placing a req if we go forward, and whether we can source an interim contractor quickly (contract-to-hire not ideal but acceptable).

If it helps, I am amenable to a partial exception (site the finance impact below). Hannah, please send the clarifications this morning and we can get this to Finance for a quick review.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Evelyn —

Thanks. Answers below and I attached an expanded org chart (org_chart_v3.pdf) with dotted lines and interim on-call owner highlighted.

1) Prioritized 12-week task list (what must ship):
- Week 1–3: stabilize KV cache regression tests + hotfix for prefix caching (required for current customers)
- Week 4–7: sharded KV cache rollout and integration tests (dependant on on-call coverage)
- Week 8–12: batching & model-parallel optimization pass A (performance uplift target 18–22%)

Non-critical (can be delayed):
- End-to-end telemetry overhaul (defer to Q3)
- Internal refactor to standardize caching APIs (defer)

2) Org chart: interim on-call owner = Priya Natarajan (senior SWE 3) with escalation to me. Dotted support from Platform SRE (team lead: Marcus Lin).

3) Enterprise commitments: Two customers (AcmeHealth, BrightFleet) have target dates in mid-May. If we defer hiring to Q3, we should negotiate a 3–4 week push with both; worst case AcmeHealth needs a pilot workaround (I have a short note ready for customer success).

Given that, my recommended path: Option B (delay backfill to Q3) if Finance can approve contractor coverage and we get a 30-day check-in to re-evaluate for earlier reprioritization. If Finance can make a one-time shift (convert contractor budget) to cover 60% of FTE in Q2 we keep critical path mostly intact.

Attachments: org_chart_v3.pdf

—Hannah
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Headcount tradeoff & backfill approval for ML infra IC

Hannah / all —

Reviewed the tradeoff sheet and the 12-week plan. Finance can support a limited accommodation: we can reallocate ~$65k of contractor budget this quarter to cover an interim contractor and approve a hiring freeze exception contingent on the following:
- A formal HC approval form signed by the hiring manager and VP (Hannah + Evelyn) — use HC_approval_form.pdf template.
- A firm 30/60/90 review cadence with measurable checkpoints tied to the three milestones you listed.
- A plan to source the contractor through TalentPartners (Elaine) and cap total spend at $70k this quarter.

If you can provide the signed form and commit to the review cadence, Finance will mark this as an approved exception (limited, for headcount onboarding only). We will need a note in the quarterly forecast to reflect the budged swap.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
